Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

1	# Terminology research pass: shared brief
2	
3	You run ONE terminology pass for the Accessible Built Environments Guidebook (`/home/user/guidebook`) for the language-and-jurisdiction pair your instruction names. It is part of a wave over the P1+P2+P3 languages. Pilot passes already exist (`terminology-pass/FR-FR/`, and DE-DE and JA-JP if finished); read `FR-FR/pass-record.md` and look at its `build.py`, which you may copy and adapt as your verifier.
4	
5	Read `CLAUDE.md` first (rules 0, 5, 7a, 8, 10; section 5 failure modes; section 7 traps incl. the Wayback route), and the three entries headed "Owner statements 2026-11-06" and the fourth in `references/project-standards.md`.
6	
7	## What this is and is not
8	- The English register is the SEARCH PLAN, not the vocabulary, and it is Canadian English from one rating instrument (RHFAC), digested in `rhfac-b651-catalogue.md` (sections 2 to 6), `rhfac-criteria.tsv` (640 criteria) and `b651-headings.tsv` (the CSA/ASC B651:23 clause structure). It is a guideline, not definitive.
9	- Rendering the register into your language produces FLAGGED, MODEL-GENERATED SEARCH SEEDS (owner OR-12b: terms you believe are IN USE in that jurisdiction, never word for word). Seeds point the reading and are never findings, never aliases, never vocabulary.
10	- A FINDING is a phrase VERBATIM in a retrieved text of that jurisdiction in its own language, with locator and a quote that verifies in the saved bytes.
11	- The register must not end where English ends: read the instrument IN FULL in its own language and record every design quantity, element, technique and defined category it treats, including ones the register lacks (reverse harvest; owner E1: a concept first met outside English is named by the instrument's own phrase, never an English gloss).
12	- Terminology only: do not extract values as findings.
13	
14	## Concept list
15	Use the 32 concepts recurring in three or more sections (catalogue 2.1), the quantity-bearing words (2.2), the base's active parameters (`select p.parameter_id, t.canonical_en from base_parameters p join terms t using(term_id)`), and the B651 clause headings that RHFAC does not name (`b651-headings.tsv`, last column). Existing aliases in your language (`select alias, alias_type, jurisdiction, notes from term_aliases where lower(language)='<code>'`) are MODEL-GENERATED SEEDS, never findings.
16	
17	## Lessons from the French pilot (apply them)
18	1. A text match is not a sense match. Record FOUND only where the instrument uses the phrase in the register concept's sense; say so in the note. "inclinaison" appearing in an unrelated sense is not a finding.
19	2. The register is criterion-shaped: near-duplicate rows share observations. Count distinct phrases as well as observations, and do not let near-duplicates inflate FOUND.
20	3. The instrument may split or merge concepts differently (the French fixed ramp is a different word from "rampe"; its corridor is not "couloir"). Record the carve difference; do not force a one-to-one map.
21	4. The drafting structure itself may differ (aim then prescription, defined categories, equivalent-effect routes). Note it in the pass record.
22	5. Held aliases that are word-for-word translations and occur in no instrument should be reported as such.
23	6. Instrument lists cannot be derived from the base for most pairs. Say how you built yours and what you could not derive.
24	
25	## Equivalence classes (owner, 2026-11-06, sixth entry in the ledger; applies to every term)
26	A concept is an EQUIVALENCE CLASS of surface forms per language and jurisdiction ("accessible parking stall", "handicapped parking", "barrier free parking", "accessibility parking", "disabled parking", "designated accessible spaces" name one concept). Do not test one form per concept. For every register concept, record all forms you find, in the instrument and, where you can, in other sources of the same jurisdiction and language (statutes, signage manuals, municipal or advocacy guidance), each with a usage type (code term, colloquial, regional variant, outdated or disfavoured, product name) and its attestation (instrument phrase with locator, other source with URL and locator, or unattested seed). Never judge a held alias wrong because the instrument you read does not use it: say "not attested by these texts" and name what could attest it. Keep disfavoured forms with a usage note. The literature also CONFLATES (one form for several concepts; several forms treated as one: accessible / universal / inclusive; lift = elevator or platform lift; ramp = slope threshold or device). Judge equivalence per occurrence by the sense the source gives the form, and where a source conflates, add a conflation note with its locator; do not settle it by fiat. Put this in an `equivalents.tsv` (concept, form, language, jurisdiction, usage_type, attestation, source) alongside the other files.
27	
28	## Procedure
29	1. **Instruments.** Primary accessibility instruments for buildings in force, current editions only, free official texts first (the national law and regulation portal, the building authority's published code). Derive candidates from `research_code_leads`, `references/standards-registry.md` and `select ref_id, pub_title, standard_number from evidence_sources where jurisdiction='<J>'`, then search. A paywalled standard you cannot retrieve is NOT-OBTAINABLE: log the attempt; do not substitute memory of its content.
30	2. **Retrieve and persist** from the repository ROOT (retrieval_log writes relative to cwd; running it elsewhere misplaces artefacts):
31	   `cd /home/user/guidebook && python3 - <<'PY'` / `import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/research'); import retrieval_log as r; r.fetch(URL, session='session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review', purpose='terminology pass <PAIR>: <what>')` / `PY`.
32	   fetch() returns None for non-JSON but persists the bytes and a manifest line under `retrieval-log/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/`. A publisher block or a JavaScript shell: use the Wayback `if_` route (CLAUDE.md section 7), as the French pass did for Légifrance. Extract text with `pdftotext -layout` or by stripping tags; save the text to `terminology-pass/<PAIR>/text/<artefact-sha-prefix>.txt` and record its sha256. Never disable TLS verification or unset the proxy. The owner has ruled that retrieved standards may be held in the repository.
33	3. **Read each retrieved instrument in full**, in its own language. Locate with scripts, read the located passages yourself, and record honestly what you read and what you did not [SKIPPED: part, why]. Image-only diagrams are unread.
34	4. **Record** under `scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/terminology-pass/<PAIR>/` (PAIR like `DA-DK`):
35	   - `search-log.md`: every query verbatim, a prior expectation written BEFORE the result, the result, and a note on query shape (R14). Keep empties.
36	   - `instruments.tsv`: title as written, issuing body, edition in force, URL, sha256 of retrieved bytes, retrieval status, read in full yes/no/partly with what was skipped.
37	   - `observations.tsv`: concept (register label or REVERSE-HARVEST), phrase VERBATIM, language, instrument, locator, context quote verbatim, text file, quote_verified_in_text, note (ours).
38	   - `coverage.tsv`: one row per register concept: FOUND / FOUND-PARTIAL / SEARCHED-ABSENT (instrument read in full, concept not treated) / NOT-OBTAINABLE / NOT-READ, with a note.
39	   - `reverse-harvest.tsv`: what the instrument treats that no register row names, in its own phrase; any gloss clearly marked as ours.
40	   - `seeds.tsv`: model-generated seeds for register concepts NOT found, flagged MODEL-GENERATED, with the jurisdiction they are meant to be in use in. Short.
41	   - `build.py` (adapted from the French pass) that regenerates the TSVs and exits 1 on any quote not found verbatim in the saved text.
42	   - `pass-record.md` (verdict first, at most 80 lines): retrieved and read, not read and why, counts by script (command beside each), where this language's instrument carves the field differently from English, method defects, and a self-attack of the five likeliest ways the record is wrong.
43	5. **Hard prohibitions.** Do not write `data/guidebook.db` or run any `db.py` write verb or migration. Do not commit or push. Do not edit `CLAUDE.md` or any file outside your `terminology-pass/<PAIR>/` folder and `retrieval-log/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/`. Invent no citation, article number, URL or quotation; every locator and quote must come from bytes you retrieved. Use no pre-reset item codes (a letter, a hyphen, two digits). Do not use the French RHFAC edition. Canadian English in your own prose; objective tone, no flattery.
44	
45	Budget: depth on the one or two principal instruments over breadth. Stop when they are read in full and recorded, or when an unavoidable block is logged. Reply in at most 12 lines: verdict, instruments read in full vs not, counts (FOUND / FOUND-PARTIAL / ABSENT / REVERSE-HARVEST), the two most surprising carve differences with English, method defects, and the folder path.

5	## 0. How to read this
6	
7	- **Guideline in approach, not exacting.** The RHFAC survey is a Canadian rating instrument: it lists criteria and weights them by points. It states **no dimension, force, slope or time**. Those live in the codes it rates against (CSA/ASC B651, the National Building Code of Canada and provincial codes), so this catalogue yields concepts and techniques to search for, never values to adopt. A criterion's point weight is RHF's weighting, not a finding about importance for disabled people.
8	- **English first is preparation, not the register.** The text below is Canadian English from one jurisdiction (CA), one programme and one author. It is the search plan for the other 13 languages of P1+P2+P3 and a seed for the reverse path: concepts that English does not name are added from native-language readings, by the instrument's own phrase (owner E1).
9	- **Two category axes, one table.** Every criterion carries technique tags and sits in a section that is a room, element or building typology. Both views in section 3 are generated from `rhfac-criteria.tsv`; neither is kept by hand. The technique tags are rule-assigned from the criterion's own words (regexes in `tools/build.py`): a lead for review, with multiple tags allowed because categories overlap by design.

141	**The overlap test is crude and over-reports gaps** (it matches word stems, so 'Headroom' is flagged although RHFAC's 'Height clearance' is the same concept in other words). **What the digest shows.** B651 frames the *exterior and public realm* far more fully than RHFAC (pedestrian crossings, intersections, transit stops, urban furniture, landscaping, temporary works, trails and beach access in Annex D), treats several technique topics as clauses of their own where RHFAC scores them as single criteria (luminance contrast with a formula and a light-reflectance definition, tactile walking surface indicators, headroom and protruding objects, door-opening force, power-assisted doors, handrail grip, slip potential in Annex B), and puts the human body into the standard through Annex A (reach ranges, walkway widths for crutch users, the detection space for a long white cane, a service dog, dimensions of wheeled mobility devices, turning areas). Clause 4.7 names functional and cognitive barriers, environmental intolerances and acoustics as 'additional considerations' in recommendation form, which is the same ground as RHFAC chapter 11 and criteria 4.5 and 4.6. Whether other jurisdictions' instruments frame those topics as clauses, as recommendations or not at all is exactly what the native-language readings must find out.

277	## 4. Beyond these two sources (leads, each [UNVERIFIED] until a source in hand states it)
278	
279	- **Named by the B651 listing but not by RHFAC:** luminance (colour) contrast as a method; tactile direction indicator positioning; platform size for platform lifts; controls and sizes of power-assisted doors; water-bottle filling stations and fountain controls; anthropometric dimensions as the basis of clearances; functional and cognitive barriers as a category.
280	- **Categories the survey scores thinly or not at all**, from the project's own vocabulary and ICF frame: sound insulation between spaces and plant noise as measured quantities; vibration; air quality and ventilation (the survey asks only that scents be absent or contained); thermal setpoints; flicker and photosensitive thresholds (the survey asks for none identified); wayfinding for people who are Deafblind; sign-language and captioning provision as a space requirement; evacuation for people who cannot use stairs beyond "area of refuge" and "evacuation chair"; bariatric and short or tall stature ranges (owner-ruled body-size frame, access need A-SIZE); tactile and haptic communication zones; ceiling hoists; adult changing facilities beyond the washroom item; queuing and timed access.
281	- **Not in either source:** building typologies the survey does not frame (transit stations and vehicles, hospitals and clinics, schools beyond "specialized learning spaces", prisons, places of worship, cemeteries, temporary event structures). Whether a P1+P2+P3 instrument frames them is a question for the native-language readings, not for this list.
282	
283	## 5. Research coverage, derived from the base
284	
285	**Principle (owner, 2026-11-06): the base sets the research coverage.** Coverage is one measure of a (concept × language-and-jurisdiction pair) cell, computed from the base and the reading records; no separate list of what has been searched is kept (rules 5 and 8). The pairs are `lang_jur_map` rows for the P1+P2+P3 jurisdictions:
286	
287	39 pairs (`select language, jurisdiction from lang_jur_map where jurisdiction in (…P1+P2+P3…)`): EN/AU, DE/BE, FR/BE, NL/BE, EN/CA, FR/CA, DE/CH, FR/CH, IT/CH, ZH/CN, DE/DE, DA/DK, ES/ES, DA/EU, DE/EU, EN/EU, ES/EU, FI/EU, FR/EU, IT/EU, NL/EU, PT/EU, SV/EU, FI/FI, SV/FI, FR/FR, EN/IE, IT/IT, JA/JP, KO/KR, NL/NL, NO/NO, EN/NZ, PT/PT, SV/SE, EN/SG, ZH/SG, EN/UK, EN/US.
288	
289	**Today:** the reading ledger (`v_scan_ledger`) holds, for the 10 active parameters only: NOT-READ 417, EXTRACTED 94, READ-PARTIAL 40, READ-NOTHING-FOUND 22, STATED-ABSENT 7. Not one of the 32 recurring concepts above and none of the long tail has a cell, because none is a term yet; and the language half of a pair cannot be derived for any source, since `evidence_sources.language` is NULL on every row (plan defect A6). **Coverage of the new register is 0 until the first native-language reading is recorded.**
290	
291	**Cell states** (proposed; the bucket table T-6b is the home): NOT-SEARCHED; SEARCHED-FOUND (phrase, locator, quote, instrument); SEARCHED-ABSENT (the instrument was read in full and states nothing); SEARCHED-QUERY-FAILED (the search shape failed, R14); NOT-OBTAINABLE (instrument held back by paywall or block, with the attempt logged).
292	
293	## 6. The terminology research pass
294	
295	This is research, and it needs passes that read instruments in their own language. One pass per language-and-jurisdiction pair:
296	
297	1. **Instrument list** for the pair: the primary accessibility instrument(s) in force, current editions only (workplan HANDOFF section 3), from `research_code_leads`, `references/standards-registry.md` and what is held. Retrieve each through `retrieval_log.fetch`; a block goes to the Wayback `if_` route (CLAUDE.md section 7); a failure is logged, not hidden.
298	2. **Search seeds.** The English register is rendered into the language as **flagged, model-generated search seeds** (owner OR-12b, third 2026-11-06 statement): terms the model believes are in use in that jurisdiction, never word for word, recorded as seeds and never as aliases. Seeds only point the reading.
299	3. **Read the instrument in full in its own language** (OR-13 open pass), not only for the seeds. For each concept found: the phrase **as the instrument writes it**, locator, a verbatim quote that verifies in the saved text, and the instrument. For each concept the instrument treats that the register lacks: the same record, in the instrument's phrase (reverse harvest, E1). For each register concept not found after a full reading: SEARCHED-ABSENT.
300	4. **Observe → adjudicate → attest** with the verbs that exist (`observe-term`, `adjudicate-term`, `add-alias` or `add-term --from-observation`); a seed whose phrase is found becomes an attested alias in place (migration 125). Rows ship in a research PR after the tooling PR merges.
301	5. **No pair is second-read before every pair is first-read**, so English does not become the frame (plan C.3).
302	
303	## 7. What this needs from the owner
304	
305	- Whether to run the first terminology passes now (research with retrieval and logging, no database rows until the tooling PR merges), and for which pairs first. Recommended: one pilot pass in three structurally different languages (Japanese, German, French) to expose method defects before all 14.

content.text: Now I'll write the throwaway read-only script that maps criteria to atomic concepts, checks label verbatimness and coverage, and prints the rows.

input.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/85c53b12-0695-5c1e-b998-83da3eff20b4/scratchpad && cat > /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/85c53b12-0695-5c1e-b998-83da3eff20b4/scratchpad/ca.py <<'PY'
# throwaway, read-only: maps RHFAC criteria / B651 headings to atomic concepts and prints rows to stdout
import csv,re,sys
B='/home/user/guidebook/scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/'
RH=[r for r in csv.reader(open(B+'rhfac-criteria.tsv',encoding='utf-8'),delimiter='\t')][1:]
BH={r[0]:r[1] for r in csv.reader(open(B+'b651-headings.tsv',encoding='utf-8'),delimiter='\t')}
DEF="Accessible, Accessible route, Adaptable seating, Amenity, Amenity zone, Braille, Cane-detectable, Change bench, Crosswalk, Dwelling, Glare, Gutter, Illumination, Intersection, Lavatory, Light reflectance value, Luminance, Luminance (colour) contrast, Michelson contrast, Passenger pick-up area, Pedestrian area, Pedestrian clearance interval, Pedestrian crossing, Pedestrian right-of-way, Pedestrian route, Permanent, Platform lift, Enclosed stair lift, Enclosed vertical lift, Unenclosed stair lift, Unenclosed vertical lift, Public right-of-way, Raised crossing, Raised intersection (or zero grade crosswalk), Ramp, Shared-use walkway, Short-term accommodation, Sign-controlled intersection, Signage, Signal-controlled intersection, Slip lane/uncontrolled access ramp, Slope, Counter slope, Cross slope, Gutter slope, Running slope, Splitter island, Tactile markings, Tactile walking surface indicator, Tactile attention indicator, Tactile direction indicator, Transfer space, Vehicular right-of-way, Visitable, Visual contrast, Walk signal interval, Wayfinding, Wheeled mobility device"
DEFS=[d.strip() for d in DEF.split(', ')]
assert all(d in DEFS for d in ['Raised intersection (or zero grade crosswalk)'])
txt={r[0]:r[5] for r in RH}; sec={r[0]:r[3] for r in RH}
# (kind,label,rhfac_regex or None,explicit codes,b651 clauses,b651 defined terms,base,tags,split_of,test,note)
C=[]
def a(kind,label,rx=None,codes='',b='',d='',base='',tags='',split='',test='',note='',secs=''):
    C.append(dict(kind=kind,label=label,rx=rx,codes=[c for c in codes.split() if c],b=[x for x in b.split() if x],d=[x.strip() for x in d.split(';') if x.strip()],base=base,tags=tags,split=split,test=test,note=note,secs=[s for s in secs.split() if s]))
Q='quantity';E='element';T='technique';S='setting';P='performance criterion';TR='trigger rule';O='outcome level';D='drafting layer'
# ---- quantities
a(Q,'Number',r'\bnumber\b|ratio mix',tags='provision_and_quantity',note="RHFAC 8.4.9 'Adequate ratio mix' mapped here (a proportion of a count)")
a(Q,'Location',r'\blocation\b|located',b='4.6.1',tags='provision_and_quantity')
a(Q,'Dimensions',r'dimension|\bsize\b|capacity',b='A.6 A.7 A.8',tags='circulation_geometry',note="carries RHFAC 'size' and 'capacity' (3.8.5, 8.1.4)")
a(Q,'Clear width',r'clear width',b='5.1.1 5.5.3 8.2.2 D.5 A.3 A.5',tags='circulation_geometry',note='TERM-002 corridor width is this quantity on a corridor or circulation route: NARROWER, so not pointed. B651 A.3 and A.5 (crutch and service-dog walkway widths) set it by user.')
a(Q,'Clear opening width',r'clear opening width',b='5.2.1',base='TERM-021',tags='doors_and_entries;circulation_geometry',split='door width',test="the clear passage through an open door or doorway, not the leaf's size")
a(Q,'Height clearance',r'height clearance',b='4.5 4.5.1 9.3.2 9.4.2 D.5',base='TERM-061',tags='circulation_geometry',note="B651 'Headroom' (4.5.1) is held here as the same object in other words (catalogue 2.4); RHFAC's '(if sheltered or parkade)' is a trigger rule, not part of the concept")
a(Q,'Running slope',r'^Slope$|low-gradient slope',b='5.1.3 5.5.1 8.2.3 D.6',d='Slope;Running slope',tags='vertical_transitions;circulation_geometry',note="TERM-001 ramp gradient is this quantity on a ramp: NARROWER, so not pointed. Conflation: DA 'stigning' is both riser height and ramp rise (kap. 2 § 57 nr. 2 vs § 56 nr. 4).")
a(Q,'Cross slope',b='5.5.2 D.7',d='Cross slope',tags='circulation_geometry',note='JA 横断勾配 (設計標準R7 pdf p.47 1.2.3.1.1) may name it; sense not judged')
a(Q,'Counter slope',d='Counter slope',tags='circulation_geometry;outdoor_and_site')
a(Q,'Gutter slope',d='Gutter slope',tags='circulation_geometry;outdoor_and_site')
a(T,'Gradation limits',b='D.6.1 D.6.2',tags='circulation_geometry;outdoor_and_site',note="B651 D.6.2 'Gradient selection' held here")
a(Q,'length',b='5.5.1',base='TERM-091',tags='vertical_transitions;circulation_geometry',split='ramp run length',test='the run limit is a horizontal length between landings',note="label is the one word B651 5.5.1 'Running slope and length' gives; read by heading only")
a(Q,'Riser height',r'riser height',b='5.4.1',tags='vertical_transitions',note="DA 'stigning' names riser height and ramp rise (conflation, recorded not resolved)")
a(Q,'tread depth',r'tread depth',b='5.4.1',tags='vertical_transitions',split='tread',test='tread measured as a depth front to back (RHFAC wording)')
a(Q,'Height',r'(?<!riser )\bheights?\b(?! clearance)|Raised dishwasher|Low mounted',b='4.3.3',tags='reach_and_heights',note='mounting or surface height above floor; the element is the other half of each criterion')
a(Q,'Reach ranges',r'reach',b='A.2',tags='reach_and_heights',note="RHFAC 'within reach' does not say forward or side")
a(Q,'Forward reach',b='A.2.1 A.2.2',tags='reach_and_heights')
a(Q,'Side reach',b='A.2.3 A.2.4',tags='reach_and_heights')
a(Q,'Knee clearance',r'knee clearance',b='6.1.6',tags='reach_and_heights',note="DE 'Unterfahrbarkeit' (ASR V3a.2 Anhang A4 Abs. 12 Nr. 2) carves the property, not the space; not judged equal")
a(Q,'Clear space',r'clear space|clear floor space|clear counter space',b='4.1 4.3.2 6.1.4 6.2.2 9.4.1',tags='circulation_geometry;reach_and_heights',note="B651 'Floor area' and 'Area allowances' held here; RHFAC 'clear space for service dogs' (8.2.5, 8.20.11) included")
a(Q,'manoeuvring space',r'manoeuv|maneuv',b='5.2.2',tags='circulation_geometry',split='turning circle',test='space to manoeuvre a mobility device, shape not stated',note="RHFAC spells it both ways: 'manoeuvring' 8.1.1 and 'maneuvering' 8.23.3")
a(Q,'Turning areas',b='A.9',tags='circulation_geometry',split='turning circle',test='an area for turning, shape not stated in the heading',note='TERM-003 turning circle names a 360 degree rotation space; B651 body not read, so not pointed')
a(Q,'Transfer space',r'transfer',b='6.4.2',d='Transfer space',tags='circulation_geometry;sanitary_and_fixtures',note="DE 'Umsetzfläche' (ASR V3a.2 Anhang A1.2 Abs. 4) may name it; not judged")
a(Q,'force',r'force|Light pressure',b='5.2.8',base='TERM-005',tags='operation_and_technology;doors_and_entries',note="B651 'Door-opening force' (5.2.8) and RHFAC 'Minimum force required to open' are this quantity on a door")
a(Q,'opening time',r'opening time|opening, hold-open',tags='doors_and_entries;operation_and_technology')
a(Q,'hold-open',r'hold-open',tags='doors_and_entries;operation_and_technology',note='hold-open time of a door')
a(Q,'closing time',r'closing time',tags='doors_and_entries;operation_and_technology',note="DE 'Schließverzögerung (Türschließer)' (ASR V3a.2 Anhang A1.7 Abs. 11) is closer delay; not judged")
a(Q,'Pedestrian clearance interval',d='Pedestrian clearance interval',tags='outdoor_and_site')
a(Q,'Walk signal interval',d='Walk signal interval',tags='outdoor_and_site')
a(Q,'Volume',r'^Volume of',tags='acoustic_and_audio',note="RHFAC 11.2.5 'traffic volume' is another sense (amount of traffic), not this")
a(Q,'background noise',r'background noise|ambient noise|noise-producing|reduce glare and noise',tags='acoustic_and_audio')
a(Q,'Illumination',r'illuminat|iluminated|lighting levels|Lighting intensities',b='4.3.7 4.6.5 5.5.6 8.2.9',d='Illumination',tags='lighting_and_glare',note="the 'Well-' prefix of 37 RHFAC sections is dropped; 'Lighting levels' (4.6.2) is this, not 'level'")
a(Q,'Glare',r'glare|reflect',d='Glare',tags='lighting_and_glare',note="RHFAC 'non-reflective surface' (7.3.1) and 'minimal reflection' (11.2.1) held here")
a(Q,'flickering',r'flicker|strobing',tags='lighting_and_glare;sensory_and_cognitive')
a(Q,'Luminance (colour) contrast',b='4.2 4.3.8 6.1.5',d='Luminance (colour) contrast;Luminance',tags='colour_and_contrast',split='contrast',test='contrast measured as luminance; B651 brackets colour into the heading')
a(Q,'Colour contrast',r'contrast',tags='colour_and_contrast',split='contrast',test="RHFAC's word: colour named, measure not stated",note="conflation: B651 4.2 'Luminance (colour) contrast' treats colour contrast as luminance contrast; recorded, not resolved")
a(Q,'Light reflectance value',d='Light reflectance value',tags='colour_and_contrast',split='contrast',test='a surface property; a contrast is the difference of two LRVs',note='TERM-011 LRV contrast is the difference of two of these: not the same object, so not pointed')
a(T,'Michelson contrast',d='Michelson contrast',tags='colour_and_contrast',split='contrast',test='a formula for contrast, not a surface property')
a(Q,'Visual contrast',d='Visual contrast',tags='colour_and_contrast',split='contrast',test='B651 defined term; relation to luminance contrast not read (body not read)')
a(Q,'Temperatures',r'Temperatures',tags='thermal_and_air',note='TERM-063 thermal comfort is an outcome, not this quantity')
a(Q,'Water temperature',b='6.5.1',tags='sanitary_and_fixtures;thermal_and_air',note='TERM-023 anti-scald valve is a device that limits it, not this')
a(Q,'sensory stimulation',r'sensory stimulation',tags='sensory_and_cognitive')
a(Q,'scents',r'scent',tags='sensory_and_cognitive;thermal_and_air',note='TERM-085 fragrance-free policy is a policy, not this')
a(Q,'sight lines',r'sight line|line of sight',tags='seating_and_furniture;communication_and_information',note='JA サイトライン and C値（Cバリュー） (設計標準R7 13.2.3.3, 13) may name it; not judged')
a(Q,'Detection space',b='A.4',tags='tactile_and_detectable',note='for people using a long white cane (A.4 heading)')
a(Q,'Changes in level',r'level change|abrupt changes',b='4.4.2',base='TERM-090',tags='vertical_transitions;surfaces_and_slip',split='level',test='level as a vertical difference between two surfaces')
a(Q,'level',r'Path is level|^Level landing|Level landings|^Level threshold|Self-levelling and level threshold',tags='surfaces_and_slip;circulation_geometry',split='level',test='level as flat or horizontal')
a(Q,'storey',r'storey|multi-level|entry level|Ground-level|multiple level',tags='vertical_transitions',split='level',test='level as a floor of a building')
a(T,'Self-levelling',r'Self-levelling',tags='vertical_transitions',split='level',test='level as stopping flush with the landing')
# ---- elements: vehicular and street
a(E,'designated accessible spaces',r'designated accessible spaces',b='9.4 9.4.4',base='TERM-027',tags='outdoor_and_site;provision_and_quantity',note='forms.tsv holds the class: owner-supplied forms and instrument forms')
a(E,'parking spaces for limited mobility users',b='9.5',tags='outdoor_and_site',note='a second class of bay in B651; JA 優先駐車区画 (設計標準R7 pdf p.52, a priority bay apart from the wheelchair bay) may be the same carve; not judged')
a(E,'Passenger pick-up areas',r'drop-off and pick-up',b='9.3',d='Passenger pick-up area',tags='outdoor_and_site',note='JA 車寄せ (政令379 Art.19(3)) may name it; not judged')
a(E,'Access aisle',b='9.3.1',tags='outdoor_and_site;circulation_geometry')
a(E,'Electric vehicle charging stations',r'Electric vehicle',tags='outdoor_and_site')
a(E,'payment machines',r'payment|Payment',b='9.6 8.6.10',tags='operation_and_technology;reach_and_heights',note="B651 8.6.10 'Parking meters' held here")
a(E,'Boarding or alighting areas',b='8.5.3',tags='outdoor_and_site')
a(E,'Pedestrian crossings',r'pedestrian crossing',b='8.3 8.3.1 8.3.2 8.3.5',d='Pedestrian crossing',tags='outdoor_and_site;circulation_geometry',note='JA エスコートゾーン (設計標準R7 pdf p.49 note), a tactile strip across a crossing, is not held here')
a(E,'Crosswalks',b='8.3.4',d='Crosswalk',tags='outdoor_and_site')
a(E,'Curb ramps',r'Curb ramp',b='8.3.3',tags='vertical_transitions;outdoor_and_site',split='ramp; curb',test='a short ramp through or up to a kerb, outside the ramp clause',note='ES Vados peatonales (TMA/851/2021 anexo art. 20) and ZH 缘石坡道 (GB 55019-2021 2.10.1) carve it apart from the ramp too')
a(E,'blended transitions',b='8.3.3',tags='vertical_transitions;outdoor_and_site',split='ramp',test='a sloped transition that the heading names apart from a curb ramp')
a(E,'Raised crossing',d='Raised crossing',tags='outdoor_and_site')
a(E,'Raised intersection',d='Raised intersection (or zero grade crosswalk)',tags='outdoor_and_site')
a(E,'Intersection',b='8.4 8.4.1 8.4.2 8.4.3',d='Intersection;Sign-controlled intersection;Signal-controlled intersection',tags='outdoor_and_site',note='the two controlled types are defined terms held here')
a(E,'Splitter island',d='Splitter island',tags='outdoor_and_site')
a(E,'pedestrian refuge areas',b='8.3.6',tags='outdoor_and_site',note="B651 'Medians' held here")
a(E,'Pedestrian crossing signals',b='8.3.7',tags='outdoor_and_site;acoustic_and_audio')
a(E,'Overpasses and underpasses',b='8.3.10',tags='outdoor_and_site')
a(E,'Speed bumps',b='8.3.8',tags='outdoor_and_site')
a(E,'Bollards',b='8.3.9',tags='outdoor_and_site;tactile_and_detectable')
a(E,'Gutter',d='Gutter',tags='outdoor_and_site')
a(E,'Slip lane/uncontrolled access ramp',d='Slip lane/uncontrolled access ramp',tags='outdoor_and_site',split='ramp',test='a vehicle lane, not a pedestrian ramp')
# routes
a(E,'Accessible route',b='5.1 5.1.5 8.2 8.2.1',d='Accessible route',tags='circulation_geometry',split='corridor',test='B651 defined route; owner 2026-10-29 (fifth): navigable by a blind person, not the same as barrier-free path of travel',note="conflation: EN-VARIANTS observations file 'Access route', 'Accessible route', 'path of travel', 'accessway', 'approach route' under one register row; recorded, not resolved")

# Register v2: atomic concepts, four new row kinds, sense splits, equivalence skeleton

Proposal for SYNTHESIS decision 3 ("restructure the register", accepted by the owner). Search plan, not vocabulary: no row, alias or term is written; rows reach the base only through `observe-term` → `adjudicate-term` in a research PR after the tooling PR (CLAUDE.md rule 10). Governing: owner 2026-11-06 entries three to six, E1, E4/OR-17, 2026-10-29 (fifth) on "accessible route".

## What changed from v1, and why
- **Criterion statements collapsed into atomic concepts.** v1 seeded passes with 32 recurring RHFAC statements, bare 2.2 words and B651 headings; near-duplicates inflated FOUND (SYNTHESIS defect 4). v2 has one row per quantity, element, technique or setting. A criterion is now the set of rows whose `seed_sources` cite its code ("Surface is firm, stable and slip resistant" ×3 wordings → firm, stable, slip resistant, Floor or ground surfaces). Values, "Well-", "if", "where" and "throughout" clauses are dropped from concepts; the conditions become trigger-rule rows.
- **Four new kinds** (SYNTHESIS 3b): performance criterion, trigger rule, outcome level, drafting layer, seeded from RHFAC/B651 where English has them ("Easy to find", "expected usage", "Visitable", B651 "shall/should/may") and from the passes' reverse harvest.
- **Group (a) concepts and group (c) sense splits** added; each split child has its own id, `split_of` (the parent word) and a discriminating test; `sense_splits.tsv` cites the phrases. Conflation is recorded in `note`, never resolved.
- **E1.** A row first met outside English has `label_en` EMPTY and carries `origin_pair`, `origin_language`, `origin_phrase` verbatim from the pass TSV. English-instrument rows (EN-CA, EN-VARIANTS) carry the wording in `label_en`; `origin_phrase` is then empty so the phrase is not held twice. Every Canadian label is a verbatim substring of a cited criterion, heading or B651 3.1 term.
- **Base cross-reference without copying.** `base_term_id` only where the row is the held term's sense; otherwise empty, with the relation (NARROWER, compound) in `note`. Each of the 10 active parameters has one pointer; the six with no same-sense row get a `base` row with an empty label.

## Columns that need a word
`kind` ∈ quantity / element / technique / setting / performance criterion / trigger rule / outcome level / drafting layer. `discriminating_test` and `technique_tags` (the catalogue's tag vocabulary) are ours, judged, not derived. `place_tags` is empty where the place derives from `seed_sources` (RHFAC section prefix → the `setting` row seeded with that section); filled nowhere yet. `seed_sources`: `RHFAC <codes>`, `RHFAC section <n>`, `B651 <clauses>`, `B651 3.1 '<defined term>'`, or `<PAIR> obs|RH · <jurisdiction> · <instrument> · <locator>` ("(in quote)" when the phrase occurs only in a context quote).

## Counts (2026-11-06; re-run from `register-v2/`, do not trust these figures)
- Rows: `tail -n +2 concepts.tsv | wc -l` → 560. By kind: `tail -n +2 concepts.tsv | cut -f2 | sort | uniq -c` → element 216, drafting layer 67, quantity 72, setting 53, performance criterion 48, trigger rule 48, technique 38, outcome level 18.
- The collapse itself (EN-CA quantity/element/technique/setting): `awk -F'\t' 'NR>1 && $4=="EN-CA" && ($2=="quantity"||$2=="element"||$2=="technique"||$2=="setting")' concepts.tsv | wc -l` → 332, from 640 criteria and 232 headings.
- Loses nothing: `python3 -I -c "import csv,re;R=[r[0] for r in csv.reader(open('../rhfac-criteria.tsv'),delimiter='\t')][1:];s=' '.join(r[11] for r in csv.reader(open('concepts.tsv'),delimiter='\t'));g={c for m in re.findall(r'RHFAC ([0-9AB.,]+)',s) for c in m.split(',')};print([c for c in R if c not in g])"` → only 12.1A.4 and 12.1B.1–5 (user-group headings and a scoring chart) and 12.3.4 (page furniture). B651 headings unseeded: the family headings 4, 4.7, 5.7, 6 and the reference list E.1–E.3.
- Non-English origin (E1): `awk -F'\t' 'NR>1 && $6!=""' concepts.tsv | wc -l` → 180. English-variant origin: `awk -F'\t' 'NR>1 && $4=="EN-VARIANTS"' concepts.tsv | wc -l` → 18.
- Sense splits: `tail -n +2 sense_splits.tsv | wc -l` → 74 child rows; parents `cut -f2 sense_splits.tsv | tail -n +2 | sort -u | wc -l` → 15.
- Base pointers: `awk -F'\t' 'NR>1 && $9!=""' concepts.tsv | wc -l` → 28. Forms: `tail -n +2 forms.tsv | wc -l` → 78.

## forms.tsv (equivalence-class skeleton)
Pre-filled only with: the owner-supplied parking forms plus RHFAC "designated accessible spaces" and B651 "Designated accessible parking" (R2-050); the qualifier class with scope notes (R2-333); elevator/lift from the owner and EN-VARIANTS (R2-163, R2-168, R2-169); and pass forms where one pass recorded two or more distinct verbatim forms of one object, curated to noun forms without values, clauses or a second object (sense as the pass judged it, re-judged in the equivalents wave). Empty `usage_type` = not yet judged. Not copied as parking forms, against SYNTHESIS 3e: PT "lugares especialmente destinados a pessoas em cadeiras de rodas" is wheelchair spectator space (PT RH, Anexo 3.6.1); JA 優先駐車区画 is a second kind of bay (note on R2-051); ES "una plaza accesible por cada 33 plazas" carries a value; US "van accessible" is a narrower class.

## Adopting-instrument key (SYNTHESIS decision 6; proposed, not populated)
A coverage cell is keyed `(concept_id, pair, jurisdiction, adopting_instrument, layer_read)`:
- `pair`: the `lang_jur_map` language-and-jurisdiction pair (e.g. de/DE, fr/BE).
- `jurisdiction`: the adopting body's level, as an ISO 3166-1 country code or an ISO 3166-2 subdivision code where the adopter is sub-national: a German Land, a Spanish comunidad autónoma, an Italian regione, a UK nation, a US or Australian state or a Canadian province, beside the federal level.
- `adopting_instrument`: the instrument as titled, with its edition in force (the Bavarian BayTB adopting DIN 18040, not "DE").
- `layer_read`: regulation (binding) / guidance (deemed-to-satisfy or advice tier) / standard (referenced or voluntary), matching SYNTHESIS defect 6. Its vocabulary must come from the column's CHECK once it exists (rule 8), never from this list.
- Cell state as in catalogue section 5 (NOT-SEARCHED, SEARCHED-FOUND, SEARCHED-ABSENT, SEARCHED-QUERY-FAILED, NOT-OBTAINABLE), so ABSENT always names what was read.

## Deliberately not in v2
The other reverse-harvest rows (route: one instrument per review, SYNTHESIS 5); user and population carves (identity lens; RHFAC 12.1B); values and RHFAC point weights; RHFAC certification levels (no TSV phrase in hand); forms beyond the pre-fill; any cell of the key; a definition for any row. Built by printing from throwaway read-only scripts that are not kept (minimise code); the tables are the artefact.

## Self-attack
1. Seeds come from regexes over criterion text, so a broad row (Height, Seating, door) can carry a wrong code. Detect: read the criterion texts behind any row's `RHFAC` codes.
2. Some merges may settle a conflation by fiat (B651 Headroom into Height clearance, Floor area into Clear space, Dressing rooms into Change Rooms). Detect: `grep -c 'held here' concepts.tsv` and judge each.
3. Policy on cross-language candidates is uneven: some get their own row ("not judged equal"), others only a note. Detect: `grep -c 'not judged' concepts.tsv` and compare.
4. Pass-origin rows inherit the passes' sense judgments, hand-set locators (DA ES FR KO) and transcriptions (IT, PT, ZH). Detect: re-run each pass's `build.py` and read the context quote.
5. The kind of a pass-origin row is mine (IT adeguamento, NL rechtens verkregen niveau, KO 상시보조서비스 could each be trigger or drafting). Detect: compare with the pass's own kind column.

The other reverse-harvest rows (route: one instrument per review, SYNTHESIS 5); user and population carves (identity lens; RHFAC 12.1B); values and RHFAC point weights; RHFAC certification levels (no TSV phrase in hand); forms beyond the pre-fill; any cell of the key; a definition for any row. ## Self-attack
1. Seeds come from regexes over criterion text, so a broad row (Height, Seating, door) can carry a wrong code. Detect: read the criterion texts behind any row's `RHFAC` codes.
2. Some merges may settle a conflation by fiat (B651 Headroom into Height clearance, Floor area into Clear space, Dressing rooms into Change Rooms). Detect: `grep -c 'held here' concepts.tsv` and judge each.
3. Policy on cross-language candidates is uneven: some get their own row ("not judged equal"), others only a note. Detect: `grep -c 'not judged' concepts.tsv` and compare.
4. Pass-origin rows inherit the passes' sense judgments, hand-set locators (DA ES FR KO) and transcriptions (IT, PT, ZH). Detect: re-run each pass's `build.py` and read the context quote.
5. The kind of a pass-origin row is mine (IT adeguamento, NL rechtens verkregen niveau, KO 상시보조서비스 could each be trigger or drafting). Detect: compare with the pass's own kind column.
